# `pointspread`

the instrument's blur at sampled vertices, read by the spatial events' chain.

Version 2, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run pointspread --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run pointspread --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run pointspread --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --kernel KERNEL --spatial-scales '["parts 4","parts 8","parts 16","parts 32"]' --reference-scale "parts 16"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `kernel` | operator inverse kernel, where {"name": "$kernel"} | yes |
| `forward` | operator forward, where {"name": "$forward"} | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | none | - |  | the recording the blur is measured for (the statistic is OF it) |
| `kernel` | `--kernel` | `none` | - |  | the inverse kernel's name, or none: the subject's one inverse kernel |
| `forward` | `--forward` | `none` | - |  | the head model's name, or none: the subject's one head model |
| `name` | `--name` | `pointspread.{kernel}` | - |  | the stored statistic's name |
| `spatial_scales` | `--spatial-scales` | none | mm |  | the spatial scales the blur is read at, as quantities (parts per hemisphere, a tile diameter in mm, a wavelength in mm or a named scale) |
| `reference_scale` | `--reference-scale` | none | mm |  | the scale whose peak the patch is cut round (one of spatial_scales) |
| `fraction` | `--fraction` | `0.5` | fraction |  | the patch is cut at this fraction of the peak |
| `vertices` | `--vertices` | `64` | - |  | the number of sampled vertices (evenly spaced in index) |
| `list` | `--list` | `[]` | - |  | the sampled vertices, stated (wins over vertices) |
| `transform` | `--transform` | `auto` | - |  | the spatial bands' transform: auto \| eigen \| chebyshev |
| `modes` | `--modes` | none | - |  | the eigenmodes used; null: the transform's |
| `order` | `--order` | none | - |  | the Chebyshev order; null: from the tolerance |
| `tolerance` | `--tolerance` | none | - |  | the Chebyshev tolerance; null: the default |
| `spatial_shape` | `--spatial-shape` | `mexhat` | - |  | the spatial level's gain: mexhat \| meyer |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.pointspread`](../nodes.md) | forward=forward, kernel=kernel | spatial_scales=$spatial_scales, reference_scale=$reference_scale, fraction=$fraction, vertices=$vertices, list=$list, transform=$transform, modes=$modes, order=$order, tolerance=$tolerance, spatial_shape=$spatial_shape | spread |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `spread` | kind statistic, name $name, of recording, axes [{"name": "source_vertex"}, {"name": "orientation"}, {"name": "measure"}] |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE INSTRUMENT'S BLUR (a statistic of the recording it is measured for): a unit current at each sampled vertex (x, y and z separately) through the head model's gain and the
kernel, read by the spatial events' chain (the power at each level of the surface's ladder on the glued cortex (made by `run glue`, the computational manifold), the patch round the reference level's peak cut at a fraction of it,
the characteristic level of its centre). The blur of THIS head model and kernel, for a source alone: many sources blur together differently.

  nxr-neuro run pointspread --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --kernel KERNEL --spatial-scales '["parts 4","parts 8","parts 16","parts 32"]' --reference-scale "parts 16"
```
